We live in a time when globalisation is rapidly encompassing travel, information, trade and investment. The internet ties people together in ways unimagined a few years ago. The globalisation of health, however, remains an elusive goal, similar to the globalisation of economic well-being. Laurie Garrett, in The Coming Plague, describes an unwelcome form of globalisation: the globalisation of disease. Garrett examines the recent history of emerging diseases such as AIDS, Ebola, Hantavirus, Rift Valley Fever, Legionnaires' disease, and others. She also explains the resurgence of familiar diseases like tuberculosis, cholera, and pneumonia as a consequence of the widespread and unwise use of antibiotics. Many of the new diseases are clearly linked to changes in land use, which brings humans into close contact with rodents or other animals that harbour viruses previously unknown to medicine and often deadly to humans. Resurgent diseases, by contrast, are a creation of our medical practice. By treating people with antibiotics without restraint, we unknowingly select strains that are immune to the antibiotics and that pass on their resistant genes to unrelated bacteria by way of plasmid transfer. The heroes of her book are the women and men on the frontlines of epidemiology. Garrett makes a plea for a greater commitment from our universities, medical schools, and government agencies to train workers who will be capable of recognizing new diseases and who will be able to move about equally well in the laboratory, the hospital and the field in pursuit of knowledge and public-health intervention around the world.

stem: What is the meaning of the word "epidemiology" in the passage?
optA: The historical study of the spread of diseases
optB: The scientific study of the spread and control of diseases
optC: The scientific study of the invention and uses of drugs
optD: The scientific study of the uses of drugs
subject: English
solution: Epidemiology = the scientific study of the distribution, spread and control of diseases. Matches option B: The scientific study of the spread and control of diseases.
context: We live in a time when globalisation is rapidly encompassing travel, information, trade and investment. The internet ties people together in ways unimagined a few years ago. The globalisation of health, however, remains an elusive goal, similar to the globalisation of economic well-being. Laurie Garrett, in The Coming Plague, describes an unwelcome form of globalisation: the globalisation of disease. Garrett examines the recent history of emerging diseases such as AIDS, Ebola, Hantavirus, Rift Valley Fever, Legionnaires' disease, and others. She also explains the resurgence of familiar diseases like tuberculosis, cholera, and pneumonia as a consequence of the widespread and unwise use of antibiotics. Many of the new diseases are clearly linked to changes in land use, which brings humans into close contact with rodents or other animals that harbour viruses previously unknown to medicine and often deadly to humans. Resurgent diseases, by contrast, are a creation of our medical practice. By treating people with antibiotics without restraint, we unknowingly select strains that are immune to the antibiotics and that pass on their resistant genes to unrelated bacteria by way of plasmid transfer. The heroes of her book are the women and men on the frontlines of epidemiology. Garrett makes a plea for a greater commitment from our universities, medical schools, and government agencies to train workers who will be capable of recognizing new diseases and who will be able to move about equally well in the laboratory, the hospital and the field in pursuit of knowledge and public-health intervention around the world.

stem: A desultory wine
subject: English
solution: Desultory, from Latin desultor meaning a circus rider who leaps from horse to horse, describes something that skips about without plan or steadiness, hence lacking consistency. Uniform is the nearest trap because it sits in the same dimension of variability but denotes the exact opposite, evenness throughout; exquisite and refined are praise words with no bearing on the headword's sense of aimless irregularity.

stem: Their apartment was adorned with the flotsam and jetsam of thrift stores and yard sales
subject: English
solution: Flotsam and jetsam are nautical terms for wreckage floating from a ship and goods thrown overboard, and the phrase has come to mean odds and ends of little value, that is debris. Keepsake is the nearest distractor because thrift store finds might be sentimental, but a keepsake is prized for its associations whereas the idiom deliberately marks the objects as miscellaneous castoffs, and treasure and gem invert the valuation entirely.

stem: We were put off by their noisome habits
subject: English
solution: Noisome derives from annoy, not from noise, and means offensive or disgusting, especially foul-smelling, so repugnant is the synonym. Salubrious is the nearest trap because it belongs to the same health and wholesomeness dimension but means health-giving, the precise opposite; efficacious and exquisite are unrelated commendatory terms. The sentence supports this, since being put off by the habits signals revulsion.

stem: The guests' convivial chatter filled the hall.
subject: English
solution: Convivial, from Latin convivium meaning a feast, describes cheerful, sociable, festive company, which genial matches exactly. Phlegmatic is the nearest distractor as a temperament word but means sluggish and unemotional, the opposite of convivial warmth; lachrymose means tearful and obdurate means stubbornly unyielding, neither of which fits chatter filling a hall.

stem: The ancient edifice enshrined a repository of arcane relics.
subject: English
solution: An edifice is a building, characteristically a large and imposing one, and among the four only bastion denotes a substantial, solid structure with the requisite grandeur, which suits an ancient building housing arcane relics. Tenement is the nearest distractor since it too names a dwelling, but it connotes a cramped, run-down apartment block, and shanty and hovel are explicitly squalid, so all three clash with the dignity the sentence attributes to the edifice.
reviewNote: None of the four is a strict dictionary synonym of edifice. Bastion primarily means a projecting fortification and only by extension a stronghold, so the item is solved by matching register and scale rather than by exact sense; tenement is the only rival with a genuine building denotation but is disqualified by its run-down connotation. Confidence is medium because the item is defective as a pure synonym question, though the intended key is almost certainly bastion.

stem: The disease caused by Trypanosoma brucei is:
subject: Biology
solution: Trypanosoma brucei is a flagellate protozoan transmitted by the tsetse fly and causes African trypanosomiasis, commonly called sleeping sickness, so (b) is correct. Filariasis and elephantiasis are two names for the same nematode disease caused by Wuchereria bancrofti, and kala-azar is caused by Leishmania donovani, so (a), (c) and (d) are all wrong.
reviewNote: Weak distractors: options (a) Filariasis and (d) 'Eliphantiasis' (sic) are the same disease under two names, so the item offers three distinct choices rather than four. The key (b) Sleeping sickness is unaffected and unambiguous, so the question still functions.

Consider the following statements:
1. Tuberculosis is caused by a virus Myocobacterium tuberculi.
2. The wuchereria bancrofti is responsible for filariasis.
Mark the correct one:
subject: Biology
solution: Statement 1 is FALSE: tuberculosis is caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, which is a bacterium (an acid-fast bacillus), not a virus, so the statement misclassifies the pathogen. Statement 2 is TRUE: the filarial nematode Wuchereria bancrofti is the agent of lymphatic filariasis. Only statement 2 is correct, giving (d).
reviewNote: Source typo: statement 1 prints 'Myocobacterium tuberculi' for Mycobacterium tuberculosis. The tested error is the word 'virus', which is wrong regardless of the misspelling.

stem:
Consider the following and mark the waterborne diseases:
I. Cholera  II. Hepatitis A
III. Typhoid  IV. Malaria
Select the correct answer:
subject: Biology
solution: Waterborne diseases spread by the faecal-oral route through contaminated drinking water. Cholera (Vibrio cholerae), Hepatitis A (enterically transmitted virus) and Typhoid (Salmonella typhi) all spread this way, so I, II and III qualify. Malaria is transmitted by the bite of an infected female Anopheles mosquito, making it vector-borne rather than waterborne, so IV is excluded and the answer is (b).

stem: Which of the following diseases is not caused by bacteria?
subject: Biology
solution: Pneumonia is commonly caused by the bacterium Streptococcus pneumoniae, typhoid by Salmonella typhi and tuberculosis by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, so (a), (b) and (c) are all bacterial. Measles is caused by the measles virus, a paramyxovirus, so it is the one not caused by bacteria and the answer is (d).

stem: Which pair is incorrectly matched?
subject: Biology
solution: The question asks for the wrongly matched pair. Athlete's foot is a dermatophyte fungal infection, rabies is caused by the rabies virus, and sleeping sickness is indeed transmitted by the tsetse fly, so (a), (b) and (c) are correctly matched. Mumps is caused by the mumps virus, not a bacterium, so (d) is the incorrect pairing and is the answer.

stem: Which of the following is a protozoan disease?
subject: Biology
solution: Malaria is caused by protozoan parasites of the genus Plasmodium, so (b) is the protozoan disease. Chickenpox (varicella-zoster virus), hepatitis B (hepatitis B virus) and rabies (rabies virus) are all viral, so none of the other options qualify.

stem:
Assertion (A):Antibiotics are ineffective against common cold.
Reason (R): Common cold is caused by a retrovirus.
optA: A and R both correct, R explains A
optB: A and R both correct, but R does not explain A
subject: Biology
solution: Assertion A is TRUE: antibiotics act on bacterial targets such as the cell wall, ribosome or bacterial enzymes, and the common cold is viral, so antibiotics are useless against it. Reason R is FALSE: the common cold is caused mainly by rhinoviruses (and some coronaviruses), which are ordinary RNA viruses, not retroviruses; a retrovirus is one that reverse-transcribes its RNA into DNA, such as HIV. Since A is correct and R is incorrect, the answer is (c).

stem: Which hormone is primarily responsible for maintaining the endometrial lining of the uterus during pregnancy?
subject: Biology
solution: Progesterone, secreted first by the corpus luteum and later by the placenta, maintains the secretory endometrium and suppresses uterine contractions, which is why a fall in progesterone triggers menstruation or abortion. Estrogen only proliferates the endometrium in the first half of the cycle and does not maintain it during pregnancy, while FSH and LH are anterior pituitary gonadotropins acting on the ovary, not on the uterine lining. Hence (c).

stem: Which part of the male reproductive system stores sperm temporarily and allows them to mature?
subject: Biology
solution: The epididymis is a long coiled duct on the posterior surface of each testis where spermatozoa are stored and acquire motility and fertilising capacity, so it is the site of temporary storage and maturation. The testes produce sperm but do not mature them, the vas deferens is a conducting tube to the urethra, and the seminal vesicle is an accessory gland secreting seminal fluid. Hence (b).

stem:
Match the following diseases with their affected areas:
A. Pneumonia  1. CNS
B. Polio     2. alveoli
C. Arthritis   3. Knee joint
D. Jaundice   4. Hepatocytes
Options:
subject: Biology
solution: Pneumonia inflames the alveoli of the lungs, so A pairs with 2. Poliovirus destroys motor neurons of the central nervous system, so B pairs with 1. Arthritis is inflammation of joints such as the knee, so C pairs with 3. Jaundice results from damage to hepatocytes and impaired bilirubin handling, so D pairs with 4. The combination A-2, B-1, C-3, D-4 is option (a).

stem: Which statement about male reproductive parts of a flower is correct?
subject: Biology
solution: The stamen is the male part of a flower and consists of a filament bearing an anther; the anther contains four microsporangia or pollen sacs in which pollen grains develop. So (b) is correct. The filament is only a stalk and produces nothing, while the stigma and the pistil belong to the female reproductive organ, the carpel, making (a), (c) and (d) false.

stem:
Consider the following statements regarding the fallopian tubes (oviducts) in humans:
1. They provide the site for fertilization.
2. They transport the ovum from the ovary to the uterus by ciliary movement.
3. They secrete follicle stimulating hormones to maintain the uterine lining.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
subject: Biology
solution: Statement 1 is TRUE: fertilisation normally occurs in the ampullary region of the fallopian tube. Statement 2 is TRUE: the ciliated epithelium lining the tube, aided by peristalsis, moves the ovum from the ovary towards the uterus. Statement 3 is FALSE: follicle stimulating hormone is secreted by the anterior pituitary, not the oviduct, and it stimulates follicle growth rather than maintaining the uterine lining. Only 1 and 2 hold, so the answer is (c).

stem: Which of the following viruses used to be responsible for highly infectious disease smallpox?
subject: Biology
solution: Smallpox was caused by the Variola virus. It was declared eradicated in 1980 by the WHO. Matches option B: Variola virus.

stem: . 'Blackwater fever' is a complication of which disease?
subject: Biology
solution: Blackwater fever is a complication of severe Plasmodium falciparum malaria in which massive intravascular haemolysis releases haemoglobin that is excreted in the urine, turning it dark red or black, and it may lead to acute kidney injury. Dengue causes plasma leakage and thrombocytopenia, cholera causes rice-water diarrhoea, and filariasis causes lymphatic obstruction, so none of them produce blackwater fever. Hence (b).
reviewNote: The stem carries a stray leading period ('. Blackwater fever') from the source.

stem:
Consider the statements about fruits and seeds:
1. After fertilization, the ovary develops into a fruit.
2. The ovule develops into a seed.
3. Fruits can be without seeds. Which of the following is/are incorrect?
subject: Biology
solution: The question asks which statements are INCORRECT. Statement 1 is true because after fertilisation the ovary wall matures into the pericarp and the ovary becomes the fruit. Statement 2 is true because each fertilised ovule develops into a seed with the integuments forming the seed coat. Statement 3 is also true because parthenocarpic fruits such as banana and seedless grape develop without fertilisation and therefore lack seeds. Since no statement is incorrect, the answer is (d).

stem:
Consider the following statements
I. The central nervous system controls major body activities by receiving information and sending responses.
II. The brain is safely protected inside the skull and is cushioned by cerebrospinal fluid.
III. The spinal cord is not connected to any body parts and plays no role in response.
IV. Nerves connect different organs to the brain and spinal cord for proper coordination.
Choose the correct option
subject: Biology
solution: Statements I, II and IV are true: the CNS integrates incoming information and issues responses, the brain lies within the cranium bathed in cerebrospinal fluid that cushions it, and the peripheral nerves link organs to the brain and spinal cord. Statement III is FALSE because the spinal cord is connected to the body by 31 pairs of spinal nerves and independently mediates reflex actions. The correct combination is I, II and IV, which is (c).

stem:
Consider the following statements.
I. A neuron is a specialised cell that transmits signals in the form of electrical impulses.
II. Dendrites receive information from other neurons.
III. Axons always carry messages towards the cell body.
IV. Synapses help transfer impulses from one neuron to the next.
Choose the NOT correct statements:
subject: Biology
solution: The question asks which statements are NOT correct. Statement III is the false one: an axon conducts the impulse away from the cell body towards the synaptic terminal, whereas it is the dendrites that carry signals towards the cell body. Statements I, II and IV are all true, since a neuron is an excitable cell conducting electrical impulses, dendrites receive input, and synapses transmit the impulse to the next neuron. Hence only III is incorrect, giving (a).

stem:
Consider the following statements.
I. Reflex actions help the body respond quickly to sudden stimuli without thinking.
II. A reflex arc involves receptors, sensory neurons, the spinal cord, motor neurons, and effectors.
III. Reflex actions always require instruction from the cerebrum before happening.
IV. The knee-jerk response is an example of a simple reflex.
Choose the correct option:
subject: Biology
solution: Statements I, II and IV are true: reflexes are rapid involuntary responses, the reflex arc runs from receptor to sensory neuron to spinal cord to motor neuron to effector, and the knee-jerk is the standard example of a simple monosynaptic reflex. Statement III is FALSE because a reflex is completed at the level of the spinal cord and the cerebrum is informed only afterwards; waiting for cerebral instruction would defeat the purpose of a reflex. So the correct set is I, II and IV, which is (c).

stem:
Consider the following statements.
I. The cerebrum helps in thinking, learning, memory, and voluntary actions.
II. The cerebellum maintains balance and coordination of movements.
III. The medulla controls involuntary activities like breathing and heartbeat.
IV. The cerebrum directly controls blinking reflexes that occur without thought.
Choose the NOT correct statements:
subject: Biology
solution: The question asks for the statements that are NOT correct. Statements I, II and III are true: the cerebrum handles thinking, learning, memory and voluntary movement, the cerebellum maintains posture, balance and coordination, and the medulla oblongata regulates involuntary functions such as breathing and heart rate. Statement IV is FALSE because an involuntary blink reflex is mediated by the brainstem, not directly by the cerebrum, which is the seat of voluntary control. Only IV is incorrect, so the answer is (c).

stem: _______ provide nutrition to the germ cells (spermatogonia).
subject: Biology
solution: Sertoli cells line the seminiferous tubules and are the nurse cells that nourish and support the developing spermatogonia, besides forming the blood-testis barrier. Leydig cells, which are the same as the interstitial cells named in option (c), lie outside the tubules and secrete testosterone rather than providing nutrition, and the vas deferens is only a conducting duct. Hence (b).
reviewNote: SOURCE DEFECT: the paper labels two options (c) and prints no (d); the fourth option text is 'vas deferens' and has been restored to position (d). Separately, (a) 'Leydig cell' and (c) 'interstitial cells' name the same cell type, so only three distinct choices are offered. The key (b) Sertoli cell is unaffected and unambiguous.

stem: Which of the following is the correct sequence of the events occurring during sexual reproduction in plants?
optA: Seedling, Embryo formation, Pollination, Fertilisation, Division of zygote
optB: Embryo formation seedling, Pollination, Fertilisation, Division of zygote
optC: Pollination, Fertilisation, Division of zygote, Embryo formation, Seedling
optD: Seedling, Embryo formation, Division of zygote, Pollination, Fertilisation
subject: Biology
solution: Sexual reproduction in a flowering plant begins with pollination, the transfer of pollen to the stigma, followed by fertilisation when the male gamete fuses with the egg to form a zygote. The zygote then divides repeatedly, develops into an embryo inside the seed, and on germination the embryo grows into a seedling. Only option (c) lists this order; the other options place seedling or embryo formation before pollination, which reverses cause and effect.

stem: Consider the following statements and mark the incorrect one:.
optA: The pituitary gland is called the master gland.
optB: It controls the functioning of other endocrine glands.
optC: The pituitary gland produces insulin that controls blood sugar.
optD: Hormones from the pituitary help in growth and development.
subject: Biology
solution: The question asks for the incorrect statement. Statement (c) is FALSE: insulin is secreted by the beta cells of the islets of Langerhans in the pancreas, not by the pituitary gland. Statements (a), (b) and (d) are all true, since the pituitary is called the master gland because its tropic hormones regulate the thyroid, adrenal cortex and gonads, and its growth hormone drives growth and development. Hence (c).

stem: Which of the following shows the correct order of phases of mitosis?
subject: Biology
solution: Mitosis proceeds in the fixed order prophase, then metaphase, then anaphase, then telophase. In prophase the chromosomes condense and the spindle forms, in metaphase they align on the equatorial plate, in anaphase the sister chromatids separate to opposite poles, and in telophase the nuclear envelopes re-form. Only option (c) gives this sequence; the others place metaphase or anaphase out of order.

stem: Consider the following statements and mark the incorrect statement:
optA: Auxins help in cell elongation in plant shoots.
optB: Gibberellins promote stem growth and seed germination.
optC: Cytokinins help in cell division and delay aging in leaves.
optD: Auxins reduce growth of shoots and only work in roots.
subject: Biology
solution: The question asks for the incorrect statement. Statement (d) is FALSE: auxin promotes cell elongation in the shoot and is in fact inhibitory to elongation in roots at the same concentration, so saying it reduces shoot growth and works only in roots inverts the real behaviour. Statements (a), (b) and (c) are true, since auxin drives shoot cell elongation, gibberellin promotes internode elongation and breaks seed dormancy, and cytokinin promotes cell division and delays leaf senescence. Hence (d).

stem:
Consider the following statements
I. Hydrotropism is the movement of roots toward water.
II. Roots show positive hydrotropism because they grow toward moisture.
III. Gravity has no role in the direction of root growth.
IV. Tropisms help plants adjust to environmental changes.
Choose the correct option:
subject: Biology
solution: Statements I, II and IV are true: hydrotropism is growth in response to a moisture gradient, roots grow towards water and so are positively hydrotropic, and tropic movements let a fixed plant adjust to its surroundings. Statement III is FALSE because roots are positively geotropic and grow downwards along the gravitational vector, so gravity clearly does influence root direction. The correct combination is I, II and IV, which is (b).

stem: Consider the following statements and mark the incorrect one:
optA: Adrenal glands release adrenaline during stress.
optB: Adrenaline increases heart rate and prepares the body for action.
optC: Adrenaline slows down breathing to save energy in emergencies.
optD: The adrenal gland is located above the kidneys.
subject: Biology
solution: The question asks for the incorrect statement. Statement (c) is FALSE: adrenaline is the fight-or-flight hormone and it dilates the bronchioles and increases the rate and depth of breathing, so it speeds respiration rather than slowing it. Statements (a), (b) and (d) are true, since the adrenal medulla releases adrenaline under stress, the hormone raises heart rate and blood pressure, and the adrenal glands sit as caps on the upper poles of the kidneys. Hence (c).

stem:
Consider the following statements
I. The pancreas produces insulin that controls glucose levels.
II. Lack of insulin can cause high levels of sugar in the blood.
III. Insulin is produced by the thyroid gland.
IV. Glucagon also helps regulate blood sugar levels.
Choose the NOT correct statements:
subject: Biology
solution: The question asks which statements are NOT correct. Statement III is the false one: insulin is secreted by the beta cells of the pancreatic islets, whereas the thyroid produces thyroxine, calcitonin and related hormones. Statements I, II and IV are true, since pancreatic insulin lowers blood glucose, its deficiency produces the hyperglycaemia of diabetes mellitus, and glucagon from the alpha cells raises blood glucose as insulin's antagonist. Only III is incorrect, giving (a).

stem:
Consider the following statements.
I. Sensory neurons carry impulses from receptors to the CNS.
II. Motor neurons carry impulses from the CNS to muscles and glands.
III. The myelin sheath helps speed up impulse transmission.
IV. Neurons reproduce frequently to repair damage.
Choose the correct option:
subject: Biology
solution: Statements I, II and III are true: afferent sensory neurons carry impulses from receptors to the central nervous system, efferent motor neurons carry them from the CNS to muscles and glands, and the myelin sheath permits saltatory conduction that greatly speeds transmission. Statement IV is FALSE because mature neurons are largely amitotic and do not divide to repair damage, which is why nerve injury heals so poorly. The correct set is I, II and III, which is (c).

stem: Which of the following roles is/are played by epididymis, vas deferens, seminal vesicles and prostate in male reproductive system of humans?
subject: Biology
solution: Spermatogenesis occurs only inside the seminiferous tubules of the testis, so any option naming it is wrong and (a) and (c) are eliminated. The epididymis matures the sperm and confers motility, while the secretions of the vas deferens, seminal vesicles and prostate together form seminal plasma that nourishes and activates the sperm, so both maturation and motility are served and (d) is too narrow. Hence (b).

stem:
Consider the following statements.
I. The tongue contains taste buds that detect sweet, sour, salty and bitter tastes.
II. Taste receptors send signals to the brain through sensory nerves.
III. Taste buds function only when the tongue moves rapidly.
IV. Smell also helps in understanding flavours.
Choose the NOT correct statements:
subject: Biology
solution: The question asks which statements are NOT correct. Statement III is the false one: taste buds are chemoreceptors that respond to substances dissolved in saliva and need no rapid tongue movement to function. Statements I, II and IV are true, since taste buds detect sweet, sour, salty and bitter, gustatory receptors relay signals to the brain over sensory nerve fibres, and olfaction contributes substantially to perceived flavour. Only III is incorrect, so the answer is (c).
reviewNote: Statement I omits umami, the fifth basic taste recognised in modern physiology, but at school level the four listed tastes are the standard set and statement I is treated as true; statement III remains the unambiguously false one.

stem:
Consider the following statements regarding coral bleaching:
1. Bleaching occurs when corals expel zooxanthellae under stress.
2. Ocean acidification reduces the ability of corals to form calcium carbonate skeletons.
3. Bleaching is always irreversible.
Which statements are correct?
subject: Geography
solution: Bleaching is the loss of the symbiotic algae, so the governing test is whether each claim matches that mechanism. Statement 1 is correct: heat or other stress makes the coral polyp expel its zooxanthellae, leaving the white calcium carbonate skeleton visible. Statement 2 is correct: acidification lowers the carbonate ion concentration and hence the saturation state, impairing calcification. Statement 3 is false because bleaching is reversible if the stress is short lived and the polyps survive, the colony can re-acquire algae. Hence 1 and 2 only.

stem:
The horizontal distribution of temperature of ocean water is largely affected by
1. Depth of water in the ocean
2. Ocean current
3. Prevailing winds
4. Latitudes
Which of the following is correct?
subject: Geography
solution: Horizontal distribution means variation from place to place across the sea surface, which is controlled by how much insolation a place receives and how heat is then moved sideways. Latitude sets the insolation received, prevailing winds drive warm surface water away or pile it up, and ocean currents carry warm water poleward and cold water equatorward, so 2, 3 and 4 are correct. Depth of water controls the vertical distribution of temperature, not the horizontal one, so statement 1 is false. The answer is 2, 3 and 4.
reviewNote: Filed under Ocean Currents because the taxonomy has no ocean-temperature subtopic; currents and winds are the mechanism the item tests. Fit is approximate.

stem: Which of the following statements with regard to the continental shelf is NOT correct?
optA: Shelves are absent to plate boundaries
optC: They have abrupt falls towards the continental slopes
subject: Geography
solution: The shelf is the gently sloping submerged continental margin, thickly blanketed by river and glacial sediment, ending seaward at the shelf break where the gradient steepens sharply into the continental slope, and it carries the world's richest fishing grounds because sunlight reaches the bottom and nutrients are abundant. That makes options (b), (c) and (d) correct descriptions. Option (a) is the incorrect one as a blanket claim: shelves are narrow along active margins such as the Chile and Sumatra coasts but they are not absent at plate boundaries generally, and the world's widest shelves are perfectly well developed near plate margins.
reviewNote: Teacher's call (2026-08-08): ships on the printed key (c). Two options are defensibly 'not correct', so the item is ambiguous as written. Printed key (c) requires reading 'abrupt falls' as a claim about the SHELF's own gradient, which is indeed gentle (under 1 degree) against the slope's 2-5 degrees; on that reading (c) is the false statement and the key is sound. But the blind derivation read 'abrupt falls TOWARDS the continental slopes' as describing the shelf break, which genuinely is abrupt, making (c) true and pointing at (a). Option (a) is itself broken English ('absent to plate boundaries'); read as 'absent/very narrow along active margins' it is a textbook truth, read as a blanket claim it is false. Key (c) retained for OMR parity; held PRIVATE rather than published.

stem:
Consider the following statements:
1. Maximum salinity is found in 20 degrees - 30 degrees North latitude.
2. The Mediterranean Sea records higher salinity due to high evaporation.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
subject: Geography
solution: Surface salinity is set by the balance of evaporation against precipitation and freshwater inflow. Statement 1 is correct: the subtropical high pressure belts near 20 to 30 degrees North and South have clear skies, descending air, high evaporation and little rain, so they record the maximum open-ocean salinity, while the equatorial belt is diluted by heavy rainfall. Statement 2 is correct: the Mediterranean is a nearly enclosed sea in a hot dry belt with restricted exchange, so evaporation raises its salinity to about 38 parts per thousand, well above the ocean average. Both are correct.
reviewNote: No salinity subtopic exists in the taxonomy; filed under Tides and Ocean Movements as the closest general ocean-water bucket. Fit is approximate.

stem:
Consider the following statements regarding ocean salinity and density:
1. The salinity of ocean water is highest at the equator due to intense evaporation.
2. An increase in salinity always leads to an increase in water density.
3. Deep ocean water has higher density than surface water due to lower temperatures and higher salinity.
4. Freshwater inflow from rivers increases ocean salinity near coastal areas.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
subject: Geography
solution: Test each statement against the controls on salinity and density. Statement 1 is false: the equator has heavy rainfall, so salinity there is lower than in the subtropical high pressure belts where the maximum occurs. Statement 2 is correct: for seawater the haline contraction coefficient is positive at all temperatures, so at a given temperature and pressure adding salt always raises density. Statement 3 is correct: deep water is both colder and slightly saltier, hence denser, which is why it sinks. Statement 4 is false: river freshwater dilutes coastal water and lowers salinity. So exactly two are correct.
reviewNote: Statement 2's word 'always' is the risk. Physically it is true holding temperature and pressure fixed, which is the natural reading of an isolated statement, giving 'only two'. If the examiner intended 'always' as a trap on the grounds that density also depends on temperature, the key would be 'only one'. Confidence medium for that reason.

stem: Which of the following areas is/are considered to be the best fishing zone in the world?
optA: The areas where cold currents flow.
optB: The areas where hot currents flow.
optC: The areas where the warm and cold currents meet.
optD: The area of the sea that is around the equator.
subject: Geography
solution: The richest fisheries need both nutrients and mixing. Where a warm and a cold current converge the mixing brings nutrients up, plankton multiplies, and the temperature contrast keeps fish concentrated, which is why the Grand Banks (Gulf Stream meeting the Labrador Current) and the seas off Japan (Kuroshio meeting the Oyashio) are the classic examples. A cold current alone or a warm current alone is less productive than the meeting zone, and the open equatorial sea is nutrient poor because of strong permanent stratification. Hence the meeting zone of warm and cold currents.

stem:
Which of the following benefits is/are related to high tide?
1. High tides help in navigation.
2. The high tides also help in fishing.
3. The rise and fall of water due to tides is being used to generate electricity in some places.
subject: Geography
solution: High tide raises the water level and therefore the depth available over bars and in harbour approaches, so statement 1 is correct: ships enter and leave harbours and cross shallow entrances at high tide. Statement 2 is correct: fish come closer to the shore during high tide, so fishermen work with the tide. Statement 3 is correct: the rise and fall itself is harnessed for tidal power, as at the Rance in France and the Gulf of Kachchh proposals in India. All three are correct.

Statement II: Earth rotates from the West towards the East once in 24 hours with respect to the Sun.
optA: Both the statements are individually true and Statement II is the correct explanation of Statement I

optD: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
subject: Geography
solution: Statement I is the standard definition of tides and is true: the periodic rise and fall of sea level results from the gravitational attraction of the Moon and the Sun together with the Earth's rotation through the tidal bulges. Statement II is also true as a separate fact: the Earth spins from west to east and completes one rotation with respect to the Sun in 24 hours. However Statement II merely states the direction and period of rotation; it does not explain why the water rises and falls, which is a gravitational effect. So both are true but II is not the explanation of I.
reviewNote: Judgement call. Because Statement I itself lists rotation among the causes, an examiner could treat II as elaborating that cause and key (a). I read II as a bare fact about rotation that supplies no causal mechanism for the rise and fall, hence (b). Confidence medium.

stem: The correct sequence of the following seas from West to East is:

optC: Black Sea, Mediterranean Sea, Caspian Sea, Aral Sea
optD: Caspian Sea, Mediterranean Sea, Black Sea, Aral Sea
subject: Geography
subtopic: World — Rivers, Canals and Water Bodies

stem:
Assertion (A): Surface currents do not move exactly in the direction of prevailing winds.
Reason (R): Coriolis force deflects moving water to the right in the Northern Hemisphere and to the left in the Southern Hemisphere.
optA: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
optB: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
optC: A is true, but R is false
optD: A is false, but R is true
subject: Geography
solution: The assertion is true: wind-driven surface water does not flow along the wind vector but at an angle to it, classically about 45 degrees for the immediate surface layer, and the depth-integrated Ekman transport is at right angles to the wind. The reason is true and is exactly the cause: the Coriolis effect arising from the Earth's rotation deflects any moving mass to the right in the Northern Hemisphere and to the left in the Southern Hemisphere, so the water is progressively turned away from the wind direction. Both are true and R explains A.

stem:
Consider the following statements regarding upwelling:
1.Upwelling occurs when surface water diverges.
2.Upwelling brings nutrient-poor water to the surface.
3.Upwelling increases biological productivity.
Which of the above statements are correct?
subject: Geography
solution: Upwelling is the rise of subsurface water to replace surface water that has been driven away. Statement 1 is correct: divergence of surface water, whether by offshore Ekman transport along a coast or by equatorial divergence, is what forces the replacement flow from below. Statement 2 is false and inverts the key fact, because deep water is nutrient rich, having accumulated nitrate and phosphate from sinking decomposing organic matter. Statement 3 is correct: those nutrients fuel phytoplankton blooms, which is why the Peru and Benguela upwelling zones are among the most productive fisheries. So 1 and 3 only.

stem:
Consider the following:
1. Gulf Stream
2. Kuroshio Current
3. West Australian Current
4. Benguela Current
Which are warm currents?
subject: Geography
solution: Currents flowing away from the equator on the western side of an ocean basin are warm, while those flowing towards the equator along the eastern side of a basin are cold. The Gulf Stream (western North Atlantic) and the Kuroshio (western North Pacific) are the classic warm western boundary currents. The West Australian Current flows equatorward along the eastern Indian Ocean margin and the Benguela flows equatorward along the eastern South Atlantic margin, so both are cold. Hence 1 and 2 only.

stem:
Which of the following is true:
1. Water with high salinity is denser than water with low salinity
2. Cold water is denser than warm water
subject: Geography
solution: Seawater density rises with salinity and falls with temperature. Statement 1 is correct because dissolved salts add mass to a given volume, so at the same temperature saltier water is denser. Statement 2 is correct because cooling contracts seawater over its whole normal range, which is why cold polar surface water sinks to form the deep water masses; the anomalous maximum density at 4 degrees Celsius applies to fresh water, not to seawater of normal salinity. Both statements are true.
reviewNote: No salinity or density subtopic exists; filed under Tides and Ocean Movements as the closest general ocean-water bucket. Fit is approximate.

stem:
Consider the following cold currents:
1. Benguela Current
2. California Current
3. Kuroshio Current
4. Peru Current
Which are correctly matched as cold currents?
subject: Geography
solution: Cold currents flow from higher latitudes towards the equator, typically along the eastern margin of an ocean basin. The Benguela along south-west Africa, the California along the west coast of North America and the Peru or Humboldt along western South America all fit that pattern and are cold. The Kuroshio is the warm western boundary current of the North Pacific flowing poleward past Japan, so it is wrongly listed. Hence 1, 2 and 4 only.

stem: Which of the following best explains why subtropical gyres rotate clockwise in the Northern Hemisphere?
optB: Coriolis force acting on trade winds and westerlies
subject: Geography
solution: A subtropical gyre is the closed circulation set up by the two wind belts that flank the subtropical high: the trade winds blowing east to west on the equatorward side and the westerlies blowing west to east on the poleward side. The Coriolis deflection to the right in the Northern Hemisphere turns the wind-driven water inward and closes the loop in the clockwise sense. Temperature gradients and thermohaline downwelling belong to the slow deep circulation, not the wind-driven gyre, and continental drift operates on geological timescales, so option (b) is correct.

stem:
Consider the following statements:
1. The rapid decrease of temperature, is called the Thermocline.
2. About 90 per cent of the total volume of water is found below the thermocline in the deep ocean. 3.Temperature decreases with the increasing depth.
4. The density of ocean water decreases with depth.
Mark the correct answer:
subject: Geography
solution: The ocean has a warm mixed surface layer, a zone of rapid temperature fall, and a cold deep layer. Statement 1 is correct, that zone of rapid decrease is the thermocline. Statement 2 is correct, roughly 90 per cent of the total volume of ocean water lies below the thermocline in the cold deep ocean. Statement 3 is correct as a general rule, temperature falls as depth increases. Statement 4 is false and inverts the relationship, because density increases with depth as water becomes colder and slightly saltier. Hence 1, 2 and 3.
reviewNote: Vertical temperature and density structure has no dedicated subtopic; filed under Tides and Ocean Movements as the closest general ocean-water bucket.

stem:
Consider the following factors:
1. Alignment angle of Sun and Moon
2. Distance of Moon from Earth
3. Rotation of Earth
4. Shape of continental shelves
Which factors influence spring--neap tide magnitude?
subject: Geography
solution: The spring to neap contrast is purely astronomical: it depends on how the solar tide adds to or opposes the lunar tide. Statement 1 is correct because at new and full moon the Sun and Moon are aligned and the two tidal forces reinforce to give spring tides, while at quadrature they oppose and give neap tides. Statement 2 is correct because the tide-raising force varies as the inverse cube of distance, so a Moon at perigee gives noticeably larger perigean spring tides. Earth's rotation fixes the frequency of the tidal cycle, roughly two highs every 24 hours and 50 minutes, not the spring-neap magnitude, and continental shelf shape amplifies the local tidal range at a particular coast rather than the spring-neap difference. Hence 1 and 2 only.
reviewNote: Statement 4 is arguable: shelf and funnel geometry strongly controls observed tidal range at a place, as in the Bay of Fundy, so an examiner reading the question as 'what controls tidal range' could key (d). I read the question as asked, the spring-neap magnitude, which is astronomical. Confidence medium.

stem:
Consider the following statements:
1. Ocean currents are the fast-surface movement of water in the ocean.
2. Ocean currents assist in maintaining the Earth's heat balance
3. Ocean currents are set in motion primarily by prevailing winds
4. Ocean currents are affected by the configuration of the ocean.
Which of these statements are correct?
subject: Geography
solution: Statement 1 describes surface currents acceptably: they are the comparatively rapid horizontal movement of surface water, far faster than the sluggish deep thermohaline flow. Statement 2 is correct because currents carry surplus heat from low to high latitudes and return cooler water, which is central to the planetary heat balance. Statement 3 is correct because prevailing winds are the primary force setting surface currents in motion, with Coriolis and density acting as secondary influences. Statement 4 is correct because the configuration of the ocean basin and coastline deflects and channels currents, as the shape of the North Atlantic does to the Gulf Stream. All four are correct.
reviewNote: Statement 1 is the only doubtful one. It contains no outright error but is an incomplete definition, since it ignores slow deep currents. If the examiner treated 'fast-surface' as disqualifying, the key would be (b) 2, 3 and 4. I do not mark a statement false for omission, hence (d). Confidence medium.

stem: Which of the following statements is true?
optA: Ocean salinity is maximum at the Tropic of Cancer and Capricorn.
optB: There is no fixed duration of tides in a month
optC: The Benguela current is a cold current of the Pacific Ocean.
optD: If the Sun, the Earth and the Moon are in a straight line then this situation is the situation of small tide
subject: Geography
solution: Test each option. Option (a) is true: maximum open-ocean surface salinity occurs in the subtropical high pressure belts near the Tropics of Cancer and Capricorn, where evaporation greatly exceeds rainfall. Option (b) is false because tides are strikingly regular, with a cycle of about 12 hours 25 minutes and spring tides twice in a lunar month. Option (c) is false because the Benguela is a cold current of the South Atlantic, not the Pacific. Option (d) is false because alignment of Sun, Earth and Moon produces spring tides, the largest, not small tides. Hence (a).
reviewNote: Mixed-topic item spanning salinity, tides and currents; filed under Tides and Ocean Movements since two of the four options concern tides.

stem:
Read the following statements about seawater density:
1. Increasing salinity at a given temperature increases density.
2. Near freezing temperatures, small salinity changes can affect density more strongly than equivalent temperature changes.
3. At high temperatures, density becomes largely insensitive to salinity.
Which of the above statements are correct?
subject: Geography
solution: The equation of state for seawater gives density a positive sensitivity to salinity at all temperatures and a temperature sensitivity that grows with temperature. Statement 1 is correct, at fixed temperature more salt means more density. Statement 2 is correct because near the freezing point the thermal expansion coefficient shrinks almost to zero, so a small salinity change outweighs an equivalent temperature change; this is why polar water columns are stratified by salinity rather than by temperature. Statement 3 is false, because the haline contraction coefficient stays large at warm temperatures, so density remains sensitive to salinity there; what changes is that temperature becomes the more powerful control, not that salinity ceases to matter. Hence 1 and 2 only.
reviewNote: Statement 3 is a distortion of a real fact, that warm water is temperature-dominated. Judged false because 'largely insensitive to salinity' overstates it. No salinity or density subtopic exists in the taxonomy; fit is approximate.

stem:
Concept of Air Mass Consider the following statements:
1. An air mass is a large body of air with uniform temperature, humidity, and pressure characteristics.
2. Air masses acquire their properties from the regions over which they form, known as source regions.
3. The boundaries between contrasting air masses are known as monsoon troughs.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
subject: Geography
solution: An air mass is a large body of air that is broadly homogeneous in temperature and moisture in the horizontal, and it acquires those properties by stagnating over a homogeneous source region such as a vast ocean or a vast plain, so statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false: the boundary or transition zone between two contrasting air masses is called a front, not a monsoon trough. The monsoon trough is the seasonal low-pressure axis over the Indian subcontinent and is unrelated to air-mass boundaries. Hence only 1 and 2 are correct, option A.
reviewNote: Statement 1 adds 'pressure' to the standard temperature-and-humidity definition, which is loose textbook wording, but the option set forces it to be treated as true: statement 3 is unambiguously false and statement 2 unambiguously true, so A is the only self-consistent combination.

stem:
Consider the following statements:
1. Tropical air masses originate in low latitudes and are warm.
2. Polar air masses originate in high latitudes and are cold.
3. When these meet, they form a frontal zone conducive to cyclone formation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
subject: Geography
solution: Air masses are named for their source-region latitude, so tropical air masses form over low latitudes and are warm, while polar air masses form over high latitudes and are cold; statements 1 and 2 are both correct. Where warm tropical air meets cold polar air the sharp thermal contrast produces the polar front, and wave disturbances along that frontal zone are precisely how temperate or extra-tropical cyclones are born, so statement 3 is also correct. All three statements are correct, option A.

stem: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes maritime and continental air masses?
optA: Maritime air masses are generally dry, while continental are moist.
optB: Maritime air masses are moist and unstable, while continental are dry and stable.
optC: Both are equally moist due to vertical mixing.
optD: Continental air masses dominate over equatorial oceans.
subject: Geography
solution: The governing idea is that an air mass takes its moisture character from its source surface: maritime air masses form over oceans and are moist, and because the underlying surface is usually warmer than the air they are heated from below and become unstable. Continental air masses form over land interiors, are dry, and typically overlie a colder surface, which makes them stable. Option A reverses this, option C is wrong because moisture content differs sharply between the two types, and option D is wrong because equatorial oceans are dominated by maritime equatorial air. Option B is correct.

stem: A stationary front is commonly associated with:
optB: Cloudy skies, drizzle, and prolonged dull weather
subject: Geography
solution: A stationary front exists where two air masses meet but neither advances, so the gentle overriding of warm air lasts for days over the same area. The result is persistent layered cloud, light drizzle or steady light rain and prolonged dull, overcast weather, which is option B. Clear calm skies belong to an anticyclone, thunderstorms and heavy showers to a fast-moving cold front, and rapidly moving air masses are by definition the opposite of a stationary front.

stem:
.Consider the following statements:
1. Warm fronts produce steady and widespread rainfall.
2. Cloud sequence is typically Cirrus → Cirrostratus → Altostratus → Nimbostratus.
3. Warm fronts are usually associated with thunderstorms.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
subject: Geography
solution: A warm front has a very gentle slope, so warm air ascends slowly over the retreating cold air and produces stratiform cloud with steady, widespread, prolonged rainfall; statement 1 is correct. The classic approach sequence as the wedge thickens overhead is cirrus, then cirrostratus, then altostratus, then nimbostratus, so statement 2 is correct. Statement 3 is false because thunderstorms come from the steep slope and violent forced uplift of a cold front, which builds cumulonimbus; warm fronts rarely produce them. Only 1 and 2 are correct, option A.

stem:
.Arrange the following stages in the correct sequence of development of an extra-tropical cyclone as per the Polar Front Theory:
1. Occluded stage
2. Mature stage
3. Frontogenesis
4. Cyclolysis
subject: Geography
solution: Under the Polar Front Theory the life cycle begins with frontogenesis, the formation of a front as warm and cold air masses come into contact along the polar front, item 3. A wave then develops on this front and deepens into the mature stage with distinct warm and cold sectors, item 2. Because the cold front moves faster it overtakes the warm front and lifts the warm sector clear of the surface, giving the occluded stage, item 1. With the warm air cut off, the energy source is lost and the system decays through cyclolysis, item 4. The correct order is therefore 3, then 2, then 1, then 4, which is option A.

stem:
With reference to clouds and the Earth's heat budget, consider the following statements:
1. Clouds reduce incoming solar radiation during the day.
2. Clouds increase outgoing longwave radiation at night.
3. Overall, clouds moderate diurnal temperature variation.
Which of the above are correct?
subject: Geography
solution: Clouds have a high albedo and reflect a large share of incoming shortwave radiation back to space, so daytime heating is reduced and statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is false and is the trap: clouds absorb outgoing terrestrial longwave radiation and re-radiate much of it downward, so they reduce the net loss of longwave radiation at night and keep cloudy nights warmer than clear ones. Because they cut the daytime maximum and raise the night-time minimum, clouds narrow the diurnal range of temperature, so statement 3 is correct. Only 1 and 3 are correct, option B.

stem: The net radiation balance of Earth is:
optA: Positive at the poles and negative near the equator.
optB: Positive near the equator and negative near the poles.
optD: Negative everywhere due to outgoing radiation.
subject: Geography
solution: Insolation received depends on the angle of the sun's rays, so low latitudes receive intense, concentrated radiation over a small area while high latitudes receive slanting rays spread over a large area and additionally lose heat by longwave emission through the year. The result is a radiation surplus in the tropics roughly between 40 degrees north and 40 degrees south and a deficit polewards of that, making option B correct. Option A reverses the pattern, option C denies the latitudinal gradient that drives all planetary circulation, and option D is impossible since the Earth as a whole is in approximate radiative equilibrium.

stem:
Temperature inversion can lead to:
1. Fog formation
2. Trapping of pollutants
3. Increased vertical air convection
Select the correct answer:
subject: Geography
solution: In a temperature inversion the normal lapse rate is reversed and warm air overlies cold air, which makes the layer extremely stable. The chilled surface air readily reaches its dew point, so fog and mist form, and the stable lid prevents pollutants from dispersing upwards, concentrating smoke and smog near the ground; statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false and is the polarity trap: stability suppresses vertical convection rather than increasing it, since a parcel lifted into warmer air above sinks back. Only 1 and 2 are correct, option A.

stem:
Statements: 1. The tropics receive more heat than they lose, creating a surplus of energy.
2. Polar regions lose more heat than they receive, leading to an energy deficit.
3. This imbalance is the fundamental cause of planetary-scale wind systems.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
subject: Geography
solution: The latitudinal heat budget shows that the tropics gain more incoming solar radiation than they lose as outgoing terrestrial radiation, giving an energy surplus, while the polar regions radiate away more than they receive, giving a deficit; statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is also correct because this permanent thermal gradient is exactly what the atmosphere and oceans work to remove: planetary wind systems and the tri-cellular circulation, together with ocean currents, transport heat polewards. All three statements are correct, option C.

Odisha, Chhattisgarh and Manipur, though all tribal-majority or tribal-heavy states, launched no such first-of-its-kind project.
reviewNote: Sources: Drishti IAS, Insights on India, Digital Health News. Distinct from the national Genome India Project.

stem: Abujhmadiya tribe belongs to which state?
subject: Current Affairs
chapter: National Events, Persons and India General Knowledge
solution: The Abujhmadiya (Abujh Maria) are a Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group living in the densely forested Abujhmarh region spread across the Narayanpur, Bijapur and Dantewada districts of CHHATTISGARH. They are a sub-group of the Gonds and speak Madi, a Gondi dialect. Odisha and Andhra Pradesh have their own PVTGs (such as the Bonda and the Chenchu), but the Abujhmarh plateau lies wholly in Chhattisgarh, and Assam is nowhere near it.
reviewNote: Sources: Wikipedia entry on Abujhmarh, Vajiram and Ravi, ForumIAS. Entry of outsiders into Abujhmarh was banned in 1980 and the ban lifted by Chhattisgarh in 2009.

Consider the following statements:
1. Acids react with metals to form salt and water.
2. Acids react with base to form salt and hydrogen gas.
3. Acids when reacted with metal carbonates, Carbon dioxide is evolved.
4. Sodium hydroxide reacts with zinc to form Sodium Zincate.
Correct code:
optA: Only one of the statements is correct.
subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Acid-Base Theory: Concepts, Oxides and Electrolytes
solution: The products of the two headline acid reactions are swapped in statements 1 and 2. An acid with an active metal gives salt plus hydrogen gas, \(\text{Zn} + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow \text{ZnSO}_4 + \text{H}_2\), so statement 1 (salt and water) is FALSE; an acid with a base gives salt plus water, so statement 2 (salt and hydrogen gas) is FALSE. Statement 3 is TRUE, since acids liberate \(\text{CO}_2\) from carbonates, and statement 4 is TRUE because \(\text{Zn} + 2\text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{Na}_2\text{ZnO}_2 + \text{H}_2\) forms sodium zincate. Exactly two statements are correct.

stem: Which of the following acids is found in Tamarind?
subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Common Acids: Names, Formulas and Uses
solution: This is a direct natural-source recall item. Tamarind owes its sourness to tartaric acid, \(\text{C}_4\text{H}_6\text{O}_6\). Oxalic acid belongs to tomato and spinach, formic acid to the ant sting and nettle, and muriatic acid is simply the commercial name for hydrochloric acid, which is the gastric acid of the stomach rather than a plant acid.

stem:
Consider the following statements:
1. All compounds containing Hydrogen are acids.
2. Carbon dioxide reacts with Calcium hydroxide to form salt and water.
3. Acids are good conductors of electricity.
4. Acids release H+ ions as anion.
How many of the above is/are correct?
optA: Only one of the statements is correct.
subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Acid-Base Theory: Concepts, Oxides and Electrolytes
solution: An acid is defined by releasing \(\text{H}^+\) in aqueous solution, not merely by containing hydrogen, so statement 1 is FALSE (\(\text{CH}_4\), \(\text{NH}_3\) and glucose all contain hydrogen and are not acids). Statement 4 is also FALSE on a definitional point: \(\text{H}^+\) is a positively charged CATION, never an anion. Statement 2 is TRUE, since \(\text{Ca(OH)}_2 + \text{CO}_2 \rightarrow \text{CaCO}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O}\) is a salt-plus-water reaction, and statement 3 is TRUE because aqueous acids furnish mobile ions and conduct. Two statements are correct.
reviewNote: Printed key (a, 'only one correct') and the blind derivation (b, 'only two') disagree, and it turns on statement 3, 'Acids are good conductors of electricity'. Statement 1 (all hydrogen compounds are acids) and statement 4 (H+ released as an anion) are plainly false, and statement 2 (CO2 + calcium hydroxide gives salt and water) is plainly true. The derivation read statement 3 as the standard textbook property and called it true, giving two. The key requires statement 3 to be false, which is defensible on the word 'good': a weak acid such as acetic acid is a weak electrolyte and a poor conductor, so the blanket claim overstates. That reading also fits the item's design, in which 1, 3 and 4 are all definitional traps and only 2 survives. Printed key retained; worth a teacher's confirmation.

stem:
Consider the following statements:
1. H+ ions can be released only in the presence of water.
2. Hydrogen ions can exist alone in the state of H+.
3. Bases release H3O+ ions when dissolved in water.
4. All the bases are soluble in water.
optA: Only one of the statements is correct.
subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Acid-Base Theory: Concepts, Oxides and Electrolytes
solution: Only statement 1 is TRUE: an acid ionises to give \(\text{H}^+\) only in the presence of water, which is why dry \(\text{HCl}\) gas shows no acidic behaviour. Statement 2 is FALSE because a bare proton cannot exist alone in solution and is always hydrated as the hydronium ion \(\text{H}_3\text{O}^+\). Statement 3 is FALSE since it is ACIDS, not bases, that give \(\text{H}_3\text{O}^+\); bases give \(\text{OH}^-\). Statement 4 is FALSE because only the subset of bases called alkalis is water-soluble, while \(\text{Cu(OH)}_2\) and \(\text{Fe(OH)}_3\) are insoluble.

stem:
Consider the following statements about Alkalis:
1. They are soluble bases.
2. They are soapy to touch.
3. They have a bitter taste.
4. They are non-corrosive and non -- harmful .
Correct code:
subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Acid-Base Theory: Concepts, Oxides and Electrolytes
solution: An alkali is by definition a water-soluble base, so statement 1 is TRUE, and the standard sensory tests give a soapy or slippery feel and a bitter taste, making statements 2 and 3 TRUE. Statement 4 is FALSE and is the only error: alkalis such as \(\text{NaOH}\) and \(\text{KOH}\) are strongly caustic, saponify skin fat and cause severe burns. Three of the four statements are correct.

stem: During a neutralization reaction:
optB: Hydrogen cation combines with hydroxide anion to form a water molecule.
optC: Hydrogen anion combines with hydroxide cation to form a water molecule.
optD: Hydrogen anion combines with hydroxide cation and hydrogen gas is released.
subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Acid-Base Theory: Concepts, Oxides and Electrolytes
solution: Neutralisation is the combination of the acid's hydrogen ion with the base's hydroxide ion, \(\text{H}^+ + \text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{O}\), the spectator ions staying in solution as the salt. The charges fix the wording: hydrogen is the CATION and hydroxide is the ANION, so options (c) and (d) invert both charges and are wrong. Option (d) is doubly wrong because no hydrogen gas is evolved in neutralisation, and option (a) mis-describes a combination as an exchange.

stem:
Consider the following statements:
1. The reaction of an acid or a base with water is an endothermic reaction.
2. Acids must be added to water.
3. Water must be added to acid.
4. The reaction of an acid or a base with water is an exothermic reaction.
Correct code:
subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Acid-Base Theory: Concepts, Oxides and Electrolytes
solution: Dissolving a concentrated acid or base in water is strongly EXOTHERMIC, because hydration of the ions releases more energy than is needed to break the solute apart. Hence statement 4 is TRUE and statement 1 is FALSE. The safety rule follows directly from that heat: acid must be added slowly to water so the large bulk of water absorbs the heat, making statement 2 TRUE and statement 3 FALSE, since pouring water onto acid heats a small volume violently and can spatter it out. Statements 2 and 4 are the correct pair.

stem:
Consider the following statements:
1. Calcium hypochlorite is also known as washing powder.
2. Sodium carbonate crystals are used as bleaching powder.
3. The chlorine gas obtained from the chlor-alkali process is used to produce bleaching powder.
4. Sodium hydrogencarbonate is used as baking soda.
Which of these is/are incorrect?
subject: Chemistry
solution: The question asks which statements are INCORRECT. Statement 1 is INCORRECT: calcium hypochlorite \(\text{CaOCl}_2\) is BLEACHING powder, not washing powder. Statement 2 is INCORRECT as well: sodium carbonate decahydrate \(\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 \cdot 10\text{H}_2\text{O}\) crystals are washing soda, not bleaching powder. Statements 3 and 4 are both CORRECT, since chlorine from the chlor-alkali process is passed over dry slaked lime to make bleaching powder, and sodium hydrogencarbonate \(\text{NaHCO}_3\) is indeed baking soda.

stem:
Consider the following statements:
1.calcium hydroxide reacts with carbon dioxide to form salt and water.
2.Acetic acid has H+ ion as cation and CH3COO- as anion.
Which of the following statements is/are correct?
subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Acid-Base Theory: Concepts, Oxides and Electrolytes
solution: Statement 1 is TRUE: \(\text{Ca(OH)}_2 + \text{CO}_2 \rightarrow \text{CaCO}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O}\), the lime-water test, in which a basic hydroxide meets an acidic oxide to give salt and water. Statement 2 is TRUE as well, since acetic acid ionises as \(\text{CH}_3\text{COOH} \rightleftharpoons \text{H}^+ + \text{CH}_3\text{COO}^-\), the proton being the cation and the acetate ion the anion, even though the dissociation is only partial. Both statements are therefore correct.

stem: Which among the following is not a byproduct or anywhere related to chlor-alkali process?
subject: Chemistry
solution: Bleaching powder, Baking soda (\(\text{NaHCO}_3\)), and Washing soda (\(\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3\)) are all made from \(\text{NaCl}\) via the Solvay or chlor-alkali process; Plaster of Paris (\(\text{CaSO}_4\cdot\tfrac{1}{2}\text{H}_2\text{O}\)) is made from gypsum. Matches option C: Plaster of Paris.

stem: Which of the following is correct for the formation of baking soda?
optB: NaCl + H2O + CO2 + NH3 → NH4Cl + NaHCO3
subject: Chemistry
solution: Baking soda is made by the Solvay route, in which brine saturated with ammonia is treated with carbon dioxide: \(\text{NaCl} + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{CO}_2 + \text{NH}_3 \rightarrow \text{NH}_4\text{Cl} + \text{NaHCO}_3\), the sparingly soluble bicarbonate precipitating out. Option (c) omits \(\text{CO}_2\) and so cannot supply the carbonate carbon, leaving the equation unbalanced in carbon. Option (a) is the hydration of sodium carbonate to washing soda and option (d) is the manufacture of bleaching powder, neither of which yields baking soda.

stem:
Consider the following pairs:
1.Sodium hydrogencarbonate --- NaCO3 --- Baking soda
2.Calcium hypochlorite --- CaOCl2 --- Bleaching powder
3.Sodium carbonate --- NaHCO3 --- Washing powder
How many of the above pairs is/are correct?
subject: Chemistry
solution: Each triplet must match name, formula and common name together. Pair 1 fails on formula, since sodium hydrogencarbonate is \(\text{NaHCO}_3\) and not the stated \(\text{NaCO}_3\), which is not even a valid formula. Pair 3 fails likewise, because sodium carbonate is \(\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3\) and \(\text{NaHCO}_3\) has been misassigned to it. Only pair 2 is correct throughout, calcium hypochlorite \(\text{CaOCl}_2\) being bleaching powder, so exactly one pair is right.

stem:
Consider the following matches between compounds and their water of crystallisation: Compound Water of crystallization
1. Gypsum two
2.Washing soda five
3.Plaster of Paris half
4.Copper sulphate ten
How many of the above matches is/are incorrect?
subject: Chemistry
solution: The question counts the INCORRECT matches. Gypsum is \(\text{CaSO}_4 \cdot 2\text{H}_2\text{O}\), so two is CORRECT, and plaster of Paris is \(\text{CaSO}_4 \cdot \tfrac{1}{2}\text{H}_2\text{O}\), so half is CORRECT. Washing soda is \(\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 \cdot 10\text{H}_2\text{O}\), so the stated five is INCORRECT, and blue vitriol is \(\text{CuSO}_4 \cdot 5\text{H}_2\text{O}\), so the stated ten is INCORRECT. The two wrong entries are simply each other's values swapped, giving two incorrect matches.

stem: Which compound, when dissolved in water, conducts electricity and forms an acidic solution?
subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Acid-Base Theory: Concepts, Oxides and Electrolytes
solution: The compound must satisfy two conditions at once: it must ionise in water to conduct, and the ions released must make the solution acidic. Acetic acid \(\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}\) is a weak electrolyte that partially ionises to \(\text{H}^+\) and \(\text{CH}_3\text{COO}^-\), so it conducts (weakly) and is acidic. \(\text{NaOH}\) conducts strongly but is alkaline and \(\text{NaCl}\) conducts strongly but is neutral, while methanol \(\text{CH}_3\text{OH}\) is a covalent non-electrolyte whose hydroxyl hydrogen is not acidic, so it fails both tests.

stem: Which among the following is the chemical formula of Hypochlorous acid?
subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Common Acids: Names, Formulas and Uses
solution: The oxoacid series of chlorine is named by the oxidation state of chlorine: hypochlorous \(\text{HClO}\) with Cl at +1, chlorous \(\text{HClO}_2\) at +3, chloric \(\text{HClO}_3\) at +5 and perchloric \(\text{HClO}_4\) at +7. The prefix hypo- with the suffix -ous marks the lowest member of the series, so hypochlorous acid is \(\text{HClO}\). It is the weak acid formed when chlorine dissolves in water and is the active bleaching species.

stem: Which of the following is the correct order of strength of acids?
subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Common Acids: Names, Formulas and Uses
solution: Ranking by dissociation constant, hydrochloric acid is essentially completely ionised with \(\text{p}K_a \approx -6\), sulphuric acid has \(\text{p}K_{a1} \approx -3\), phosphorous acid \(\text{H}_3\text{PO}_3\) has \(K_{a1} \approx 10^{-2}\) and acetic acid is the weakest at \(K_a = 1.8 \times 10^{-5}\). That gives \(\text{HCl} > \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 > \text{H}_3\text{PO}_3 > \text{CH}_3\text{COOH}\), which is option (d). Option (c) is wrong because phosphoric acid \(K_{a1} = 7.5 \times 10^{-3}\) is stronger than acetic acid, not weaker, and option (b) wrongly places acetic acid above phosphorous acid.
reviewNote: Options (a) and (d) differ ONLY in the HCl versus H2SO4 order, so this hinges on one comparison. On dissociation-constant grounds HCl (pKa about -6) is roughly a thousand times stronger than sulphuric acid (pKa1 about -3), and the standard strong-acid series HClO4 > HI > HBr > HCl > H2SO4 > HNO3 places HCl above H2SO4, so (d) is the defensible answer. Flagging medium confidence because a setter following the common Indian school claim that sulphuric acid is the strongest mineral acid would key (a) instead.

stem: Which among the following are dibasic and tribasic acids respectively?
subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Common Acids: Names, Formulas and Uses
solution: Basicity counts the REPLACEABLE hydrogens, that is those bonded to oxygen and released as \(\text{H}^+\). Sulphuric acid \(\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4\) releases two protons and is dibasic, while phosphoric acid \(\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4\) has three \(\text{P-OH}\) groups and is tribasic, so option (d) matches the required order. Options (a) and (b) both name monobasic acids first, hydrochloric and nitric, and option (c) reverses the order by naming the tribasic acid first. Note the contrast that phosphorous acid \(\text{H}_3\text{PO}_3\) is only DIBASIC despite three hydrogens, because one hydrogen is bonded directly to phosphorus and is not ionisable, but the option here names phosphoric acid, which genuinely is tribasic.

stem: The pH of coffee is(approx.) :
subject: Chemistry
solution: Coffee is mildly acidic because of chlorogenic, quinic and citric acids, and brewed black coffee measures roughly pH 4.85 to 5.10. Of the four options only 4.25 and 6.85 are in the mildly acidic region, and 4.25 is much closer to the true value than 6.85, which is nearly neutral. Option (c) at 1.25 is gastric-acid territory and option (d) at 10.03 is alkaline, so both are far outside range.

Consider the following matches:

Compound | Nature
---|---
A. Aluminium oxide | 1. Amphoteric
B. Calcium oxide | 2. Strong acid
C. Acetic acid | 3. Alkali
D. Sodium hydroxide | 4. Weak acid
E. Hydrochloric acid | 5. Base
subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Acid-Base Theory: Concepts, Oxides and Electrolytes
solution: Working the pairing out independently: aluminium oxide \(\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3\) dissolves in both acid and alkali, so it is amphoteric (1); calcium oxide is a basic oxide, hence base (5); acetic acid is only partially ionised, hence weak acid (4); sodium hydroxide is a water-soluble base, hence alkali (3); and hydrochloric acid is fully ionised, hence strong acid (2). That gives A-1, B-5, C-4, D-3, E-2, which is option (b). The distinction that decides between the distractors is that calcium oxide is a base but not an alkali, while sodium hydroxide is the soluble base and therefore takes the alkali slot.
reviewNote: The four options are printed as a 2-column table, so they appear in the order a, c, b, d on the page; re-ordered to a/b/c/d here. Independently derived pairing (aluminium oxide amphoteric, calcium oxide base, acetic acid weak acid, sodium hydroxide alkali, hydrochloric acid strong acid) confirms the printed key (b).

stem: The pH of the solution obtained by dissolving pure calcium chloride in water is:
subject: Chemistry
solution: The pH of a salt solution is fixed by the parentage of its ions. Calcium chloride comes from the strong base \(\text{Ca(OH)}_2\) and the strong acid \(\text{HCl}\), so neither \(\text{Ca}^{2+}\) nor \(\text{Cl}^-\) hydrolyses to any appreciable extent and no excess \(\text{H}^+\) or \(\text{OH}^-\) is generated. The solution therefore stays neutral at about pH 7. A salt would only test acidic if it came from a weak base and a strong acid, or basic in the reverse case.

stem: What is a constellation?
optA: A particular pattern of equidistant stars from the earth in the sky
optB: A particular pattern of stars that may not be equidistant from the earth in the sky
optC: A particular pattern of planets of our solar system in the sky
optD: A particular pattern of stars, planets and satellites in the sky due to their position in the space
subject: Geography
chapter: Earth in Space, Maps and Coordinates
solution: A constellation is a recognisable pattern that stars appear to form when projected on the sky as seen from Earth, such as Orion or Ursa Major. The stars in one constellation are usually at wildly different distances from Earth and are not physically associated; the pattern is a line-of-sight effect, so option (a) is wrong and option (b) is right. Constellations are made of stars, not planets or satellites, which merely wander across them, so options (c) and (d) are wrong.
reviewNote: Astronomy item placed under the Earth in Space chapter as instructed; 'Planets and Solar System' is the nearest listed subtopic, though a constellation is neither.

stem: Which of the following is based on the principle of nuclear fusion?
subject: Physics
solution: Nuclear fusion is the joining of light nuclei such as isotopes of hydrogen into a heavier nucleus, which requires temperatures of millions of degrees to overcome Coulomb repulsion. The hydrogen bomb, or thermonuclear bomb, uses a fission trigger to create those conditions and then releases its main energy by fusing deuterium and tritium, so option B is correct. The atomic bomb works by uncontrolled chain-reaction fission of heavy nuclei such as uranium-235 or plutonium-239, so it is not fusion-based, which rules out options A, C and D.

stem: Cement is formed by strongly heating a mixture of:
subject: Chemistry
solution: Portland cement is made by strongly heating a ground mixture of limestone \(\text{CaCO}_3\) with clay in a rotary kiln at roughly 1500 degrees Celsius, producing clinker that is then ground with a little gypsum. Limestone supplies the calcium oxide while clay supplies the silica, alumina and iron oxide that form the calcium silicates. Graphite is pure carbon used in pencils, electrodes and lubricants and has no role in cement manufacture, so options (a), (c) and (d) are all ruled out.

stem: Which one of the following instruments is used for measuring moisture content of air?
subject: Physics
solution: Moisture content of air, that is humidity, is measured by a hygrometer, so option B is correct; the wet-and-dry-bulb psychrometer is its common form. The distractors are deliberate near-misses on the name: a hydrometer measures the relative density or specific gravity of a liquid, a hypsometer measures altitude by determining the boiling point of water, and a pycnometer is a fixed-volume flask used to measure the density of a liquid or solid. None of these measures atmospheric moisture.
reviewNote: Taxonomy fit is awkward. This is an instrument-identification recall item with no measurement-of-a-quantity content, so it sits under Units, Measurement and Dimensions / Units and Dimensions only as the closest available home per the brief; the alternative Modern Physics / Scientific Acronyms is a worse fit since no acronym is involved.

stem: Where is the headquarters of UNESCO?
subject: Current Affairs
solution: UNESCO, the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization founded in 1945, is headquartered at Place de Fontenoy in PARIS, France. New York hosts the UN Secretariat, Geneva hosts bodies such as WHO, ILO and WTO, and Brussels is the seat of the EU and NATO, none of which is UNESCO.
reviewNote: Standard static general knowledge; no ambiguity.
